title: Universal Consciousness Editorial Team
excerpt: The staff desk that writes, edits, and corrects Universal Consciousness. This profile does not claim personal clinical or lineage credentials.

quick_answer.question: Who writes Universal Consciousness?
quick_answer.answer: Pages are written by the Universal Consciousness Editorial Team, a staff desk. The byline is not a named guru, physician, or lineage holder, and it does not imply a personal credential.

intro:
Universal Consciousness publishes explainers, guides, glossary entries, and question pages about meditation, consciousness, and Indian philosophical traditions. The byline on those pages is a desk, not a fictional expert.

This profile exists so readers can see who is responsible for the words. Responsibility sits with the publication. It does not sit with an invented biography.

sections.heading: What does this byline mean?
sections.content:
The Universal Consciousness Editorial Team is the name of the staff desk that researches, drafts, and revises the publication. A page signed by the desk has been prepared as reference writing for a general reader in the United States.

The desk is not a person with a degree, a clinical license, or an initiation that this site can verify. Those details are omitted because they would be fiction. If a named writer later contributes, that writer will receive a separate profile, and the profile will list only experience that can be checked.

sections.heading: What does the desk cover?
sections.content:
The desk covers consciousness, meditation, mindfulness, spirituality, yoga, kundalini, chakras, reiki, Ayurveda, mantras, breathwork, Vedanta, and related terms in the [glossary](/glossary/). The aim is to explain how a tradition talks, where the talk comes from, and what a careful reader should not infer.

Health-adjacent subjects are handled with a standing distinction. A traditional claim is labeled as tradition. A practitioner report is labeled as report. A research finding is cited to a public source such as the National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health or a published review. The three are not blended into a promise.

sections.heading: How are pages revised?
sections.content:
A published date marks the first public version. A modified date changes only when the page itself changes in substance. Dates are not refreshed to make an old page look new.

Corrections are described on the [corrections](/corrections/) page. Readers can write to the desk through the [contact](/contact/) page. The [editorial policy](/editorial-policy/) explains source standards and the limited way software may assist drafting.

key_takeaways: The byline names a staff desk, not a credentialed individual.
Named contributors will be added only with checkable biographies.
Health and spiritual claims stay separated into tradition, report, and evidence.

faq.question: Is the editorial team a specific teacher?
faq.answer: No. The name refers to the publication's staff desk. It should not be read as a lineage title or a clinical qualification.

faq.question: Can I request a correction?
faq.answer: Yes. Use the contact address on the contact page and include the URL, the sentence you dispute, and a source if you have one.
